doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Avoiding contemporary jazz and developing her own sound
summary: She came to jazz in the early 90s, skipped contemporary jazz and transcribing, and wanted an individual bass sound.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: When you think of jazz, what was current, gee by the time you — it must have been early 80s when you started becoming aware of jazz — is that true?
Well not really no, because I didn’t start until I was eight and that was in 1985. I didn’t really get into the jazz until the early 90s maybe.
Oh, gee, all right. So what’s current then? Humm. That’s only like seven or eight years ago.
Did you ever get into what, for lack of a better term nowadays is called contemporary jazz, the Kenny G type of thing?

No. I wasn’t really involved with that. Because my brother had given me tapes of a lot of older styles of music but I didn’t actually go out and actively seek to listen to jazz. Because it wasn’t something I was really interested in until my sophomore year of high school. You know I enjoyed it but I wasn’t actively involved with it. After my sophomore year, and I started to begin to play a lot more, I was concerned about not wanting to sound like a lot of other bass players. I wanted my own individual sound. So I didn’t do a lot of listening at first. I didn’t learn a lot of history either. I just kind of like played and tried to develop my own sound. So I didn’t listen to the contemporary stuff, not a lot of listening, no.
That was a conscious decision on your part? That you didn’t want to become a copy cat of someone else?

Right. Because a lot of people had said well transcribe these solos or these bass lines. And I understand why they say that, it’s a good idea to get the style of a certain player. But I didn’t want to be copying lines from it. No I wanted to try to bring my own sound to the music.
